items.question: Under what conditions must this teaching be kept concealed?
premises: The teaching is to be concealed
Concealment requires deliberate effort
The context is the mortal world among lowest men
items.inference: This teaching must be carefully hidden in the mortal world among unworthy people.
items.plain_english: It must be carefully concealed in the mortal world among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom may this teaching rightly be given?
premises: The teaching is to be given
The recipient must be previously accomplished
The recipient must be tested for one year
items.inference: This teaching may be given only to a previously accomplished person tested for one year.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is already accomplished and has been tested for one year.

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text emerged from Candradvīpa
The section is identified as fifth
The section is a chapter
items.inference: The fifth chapter concludes in the work emerged from Candradvīpa.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the work that emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: By whose grace has the determination of Kaula become known?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas
Knowledge arose by that lord's grace
The object known is the determination of Kaula
items.inference: The determination of Kaula has become known to the speaker by the grace of the lord of Kaulas.
items.plain_english: O lord of the Kaulas, by your grace I have come to know the determination of Kaula.

items.question: What is the declared identity and essential nature of the soul?
premises: The soul is said to be declared
Its identity is questioned
Its essential nature is questioned
items.inference: The inquiry seeks both the identity and the essential nature of the declared soul.
items.plain_english: Who is that soul that has been declared, and what is the true nature of the soul?

items.question: Into what does the soul dissolve, and what explains this fully?
premises: The soul's dissolution is questioned
A specific locus of dissolution is sought
A complete explanation is requested
items.inference: The speaker asks for a full explanation of where the soul dissolves.
items.plain_english: And into what does it dissolve? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What supreme qualities define the true nature of that reality?
premises: That reality is supreme
It is partless and eternal
It is free from disease and stainless
items.inference: The reality in question is defined as supreme, partless, eternal, and pure.
items.plain_english: He is supreme, partless, eternal, free from affliction, and stainless.

items.question: How is the supreme soul identified in terms of haṃsa and individuality?
premises: The soul is described as supreme
That same soul is identified as haṃsa
It is characterized as power and individual
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified as the haṃsa, characterized as power and individual.
uncertainties: The precise sense of śakti+pudgalaḥ is doctrinally compressed.
items.plain_english: That soul is supreme; indeed, he is the haṃsa, the individual endowed with power.

items.question: Where is the breath-filled vital air said to be situated?
premises: The vital air is filled with breath
It is described as situated
Its location is in all beings
items.inference: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.
uncertainties: Agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam is irregular in the given form.
items.plain_english: The breath-filled vital air is situated in all living beings.

items.question: What is the soul called immediately upon leaving the body?
premises: The condition is merely leaving the body
At that moment a designation is given
The designation is supreme Śiva
items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, that soul is called supreme Śiva.
items.plain_english: As soon as it leaves the body, it is called the supreme Śiva.

items.question: How is this teaching transmitted and received according to tradition?
premises: The teaching is heard in the ear
It comes through successive tradition
The goddess is addressed as recipient
items.inference: This teaching is received orally, having come down through traditional succession.
items.plain_english: O goddess, it is heard in the ear, having come down through the succession of tradition.

items.question: What is the effect of merely hearing this knowledge?
premises: The means is this knowledge alone
The knowledge is merely heard
The fair-faced one is addressed
items.inference: Even merely hearing this knowledge has a significant effect.
uncertainties: The result is completed in the following verse.
items.plain_english: O fair-faced one, by merely hearing this knowledge...

items.question: What disciplined practice over six months leads toward freedom from bondage?
premises: Practice is enjoined for six months
The practitioner undertakes the ochre discipline
The state is free from bondage
items.inference: One who practices this bondage-free ochre discipline for six months advances toward liberation.
uncertainties: kāṣāyaṃ may refer to ochre renunciation or a related discipline.
items.plain_english: Whoever practices this bondage-free ochre discipline for six months...

items.question: What result follows the prescribed practice in relation to disease and yogis?
premises: The practitioner becomes freed from all diseases
The practitioner attains union
The union is with yogis
items.inference: The prescribed practice results in freedom from all diseases and union with yogis.
items.plain_english: ...becomes freed from all diseases and attains union with the yogis.

items.question: What teaching about the soul's practice has now been communicated to Bhairavī?
premises: A teaching has been told
The recipient is Bhairavī
The topic is the practice of the soul
items.inference: The practice concerning the soul has now been communicated to Bhairavī.
items.plain_english: O Bhairavī, this practice concerning the soul has been told to you.

items.question: What kind of resolved recipient is fit to receive this teaching?
premises: The teaching is to be given
The recipient is endowed with all states
The recipient has a resolved mind
items.inference: This teaching should be given to a resolved person endowed with all states.
uncertainties: The exact sense of sarva+bhāva+upapannasya is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: It should be given to one who is endowed with all states and has a firmly resolved mind.

items.question: Why must the Kaula essence originating from the yoginīs not be given indiscriminately?
premises: The Kaula essence is identified
Its origin is from the yoginīs
Giving it is explicitly prohibited
items.inference: The Kaula essence originating from the yoginīs must not be given indiscriminately.
items.plain_english: The Kaula essence, which originates from the yoginīs, must not be given.

items.question: What transformation of the body is claimed after ignorance's veil is struck away?
premises: The body was struck by the veil of ignorance
A present change is asserted today
The body is now described as pure
items.inference: The body, once struck by ignorance, is now claimed to be pure.
items.plain_english: Today my body, once struck by the veil of ignorance, is pure.

items.question: What auspicious teaching about overcoming time is now sought?
premises: The speaker expresses a wish now
The wish is to hear a teaching
The teaching concerns overcoming time
items.inference: The speaker now seeks the auspicious teaching on overcoming time.
uncertainties: vañcanaṃ can mean deception or outwitting; context suggests overcoming.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious teaching on overcoming time.

items.question: What assurance is given about the destruction of death through this teaching?
premises: The speaker promises to tell
There is no doubt
Death is said to be destroyed
items.inference: The teaching is assured to explain how death is destroyed without doubt.
items.plain_english: I will tell you, without doubt, how death is destroyed.

items.question: How can even a wise person be affected at the point of nectar?
premises: The locus is the tip of nectar
There is burning by the essence of juice
Even a wise person is affected
items.inference: Even a wise person can experience burning at the point of nectar by its essence.
uncertainties: The imagery is esoteric and may refer to yogic physiology.
items.plain_english: Even a wise person may be burned at the tip of nectar by the essence of its juice.

items.question: What yogic technique involving breath should be performed slowly at the palate's root?
premises: The locus is the root of tongue and palate
The practitioner places and draws in air
The action should be done slowly
items.inference: One should slowly draw in the breath at the root of the tongue and palate.
items.plain_english: Placing it at the root of the tongue and palate, one should slowly drink in the breath.

items.question: What result follows from practicing this technique for one year?
premises: The practice is continued for one year
The condition is sustained practice
Old age and death are destroyed
items.inference: When practiced for one year, this technique destroys old age and death.
items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: What protection against poison is claimed for the practitioner's body?
premises: Poison does not enter the body
This holds even if bitten
The biting may be by great serpents
items.inference: The practitioner's body becomes immune to poison even from great serpent bites.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
